extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH K99/R00 (R00) pilot clinical trial applications and institutional research teams (PIs, study personnel, IRB contacts)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for designing, protecting, monitoring, and reporting a pilot randomized behavioral intervention trial (K99/R00 R00 portion) testing a dementia-enhanced training and tool for home hospice clinicians. Covers human subjects protection, data safety/monitoring, recruitment/enrollment, outcomes, statistics/power, dissemination, and data sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data storage and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: All data will be centrally stored at WCM on a secure server in a folder that can only be accessed by credentialed study personnel on password-protected computers; a separate file linking interview participants’ names and study ID numbers will also be stored on the secure server and will be password-protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper transcripts with participant identifiers stored in locked file cabinet in a locked office; electronic/digital data on secure server or password-protected RedCap account; all data coded with unique participant identification numbers and participant names/identifiers not recorded on study materials; only authorized study personnel have access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data monitoring procedures and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracking forms will be developed to document when the review of study data occurs. Dr. Luth will review all consent forms as they are received. Participant recruitment and enrollment will be recorded by the study Research Assistant who will generate a weekly report for Dr. Luth to review. Dr. Luth will review self-report measures for completeness and accuracy of entry into RedCap on a weekly basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All data will be reviewed semi-annually by Dr. Luth and her mentorship team; the study protocol and results will be reviewed annually by the WCM IRB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse event identification and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The study Research Assistant or PI may become aware of adverse events through participant self-report or interactions with participants. Dr. Luth will report any adverse events with caregiver or clinician participants to the WCM IRB and/or federal agencies and with VNSNY clinician interview participants to the VNSNY IRB and/or federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All adverse events noted by study personnel will be discussed with Dr. Luth and reported within 24 hours of discovery to the IRB(s); Dr. Luth will discuss safety concerns, adverse events, participant complaints, and protocol violations with the full research team; all study personnel will have completed NIH-required human subjects training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All caregiver and clinician participants will be required to provide written informed consent before being enrolled in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informed consent will be conducted by trained study personnel who will review procedures in detail, allow questions, emphasize participant rights (including right to withdraw at any time), and include a section explaining protected health information and confidentiality per HIPAA, plus contact information for PI and relevant IRB and Privacy Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against risk and protocol adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the auspices of the WCM and VNSNY IRBs, participants will be protected by strict adherence to study protocols governing participant safety, data privacy, informed consent, withdrawal without prejudice, and immediate reporting to the PI and the IRBs of any adverse events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research data maintained in secure environment; only authorized personnel access data; written materials in locked cabinets; electronic data on secure servers; confidentiality limits disclosed; confidentiality may be suspended in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling participant distress and disclosure (referral & reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Caregivers may experience emotional distress from completing assessments; participants who exhibit distress will be encouraged to speak with their primary care physician or call Eldercare Locator; in more severe cases, a social worker and/or psychiatrist will be consulted and participant referred to appropriate level of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If abuse, suicidal ideation, or psychological distress is uncovered, a social worker and/or psychiatrist will be contacted immediately; cases of suspected abuse will be reported to the patient’s primary care physician and/or practice social worker; participants will be informed of limits to confidentiality during consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerable subjects policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Not applicable to this study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission explicitly states vulnerable subjects are not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women and minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: No participants will be excluded on the basis of gender or race/ethnicity; enrollment expectations are provided (e.g., overall sample expected 70-80% female; estimates of racial/ethnic composition are given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given disproportionate impact on African-American persons, the study will sample equal numbers of African-American and white family caregivers; clinicians will not be excluded by race/ethnicity; estimates for racial/ethnic composition and Hispanic percentage are provided and justified with workforce and prior research data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion of children and age limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals under 18 years of age will not be included in this research; clinicians must be over 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age limits listed: Min Age 19 Years, Max Age 90 Years (for relevant participant categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria (clinicians and family caregivers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinicians: nurse or social worker who provides home hospice care to patients with primary or co-morbid diagnoses of Alzheimer's Disease and related dementias; Family caregivers: family member who provides care to a community-dwelling patient with primary or co-morbid dementia who has been enrolled in home hospice care for more than 7 days; targeted races for caregivers: African American or white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility criteria specify roles, patient diagnoses, and minimum hospice enrollment duration (>7 days) for caregivers used to reduce attrition and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment targets and cluster randomization plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit 40 clinician participants from four existing VNSNY hospice teams (≈10 clinicians/team); randomize two teams to intervention (n=20 clinicians) and two teams to control (n=20 clinicians). Enroll 4 family caregivers (2 African American, 2 white) for each of the 40 clinicians (n=160 family caregivers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomization occurs at the clinician (cluster) level; clinicians and their patients are assigned to the same group; recruitment steps involve VNSNY identifying eligible patients and caregivers already on clinicians’ caseloads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize attrition of family caregivers due to patient death and reduce burden, intervention delivery will be limited to caregivers of patients who have been in hospice for longer than one week; interventions will be delivered in convenient locations and amount of data collected will be minimized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators will explain importance of continued involvement and potential benefits; data collection timing is planned after initial transition to hospice; dissemination of findings to participants who request them is planned as an incentive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study timeline and IRB approvals before recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: IRB applications will be submitted at sponsoring institution and VNSNY during Quarter 2, Year 4 of the award; once IRB approval is obtained, participant recruitment for pilot testing will begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline includes K99 and R00 phases, manuscript preparation, and a plan to prepare an R01 application in Year 5; activities and aims mapped to quarters/years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Will a Data and Safety Monitoring Board be appointed for this study? No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application explicitly selects 'No' for DSMB appointment and includes a Data and Safety Monitoring Plan document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and secondary outcome measures (measurement timing and instruments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary: Family Caregiver Burden measured at baseline and visits 2–4 using the validated 12-item Zarit Caregiver Burden Inventory. Other: Clinician knowledge of dementia-related issues at end of life (baseline, post-intervention) using a revised Dementia Knowledge Assessment Scale and tailored assessment questions; Patient hospice discharge status (3 and 6 months post-intervention) assessed as deceased vs alive, reported by caregiver and verified in electronic records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome descriptions include time frames and brief descriptions of measurement approaches and verification via electronic hospice records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical design and power rationale for pilot RCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary analyses proposed as a full information mixed model approach; primary power calculations conservatively based on two-group comparison of endpoint means with possible attrition. Sample sizes: clinicians n=40 (20 per group); family caregivers n=160 (80 per group); power assumed 0.80.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions specified: variance=9.8 for ZBI, alpha=0.05, reliability=0.9, cluster VIF estimated (Vif=1.09) with ICC=0.03 and cluster size Nc=4; detectable effect sizes (Cohen’s d) around 0.38–0.49 depending on correlation between waves; sample size justification references pilot study recommendations and specific formula adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization unit and intervention model
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention model: Parallel. Masking: No. Allocation: Randomized. Randomization occurs at clinician level because training and tool are designed to change clinician knowledge and approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants (family caregivers) are assigned to the same group as their clinician; study phase labeled 'Other / behavioral intervention' and is not an NIH-defined Phase III clinical trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of subject participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject participation duration: Up to two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified under Section 4.5; informs scheduling of baseline, follow-up visits, and timeframe for intervention testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClinicalTrials.gov registration and reporting responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Luth will register the trial prior to enrolling the first subject and will be responsible for complying with ClinicalTrials.gov requirements, including results reporting and Adverse Events reporting upon project conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WCM ClinicalTrials.gov administrator will facilitate dissemination through registration and reporting; PI responsible for accuracy, content updates, problem resolution, and ensuring informed consent documents include statement related to posting on ClinicalTrials.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource and data sharing plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual property and data generated will be disseminated in accordance with WCM and NIH policies, including NIH Data Sharing Policy; types of data to be generated include audio-recordings of semi-structured interviews and focus groups, self-report demographics, knowledge measures, caregiver burden measures, discrimination, and perceptions of feasibility/utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Luth and her team have agreed to specific plans for data sharing, resources, tools, and other intellectual property related to the application; data will be coded and identifiers kept separately and securely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic records for eligibility screening and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Solely for identifying potentially eligible family caregivers, data from VNSNY electronic hospice records (age, ethnicity, functional and cognitive status, date of hospice enrollment, caregiver contact) will be obtained; hospice records will also be checked for patient discharge status to verify caregiver reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information will not be used or analyzed elsewhere in the study beyond identifying participation eligibility; information about potentially eligible caregivers will be shared via secure file transfer system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of highly sensitive detections (abuse, suicidal ideation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a rare possibility of uncovering abuse within a patient-caregiver relationship; such cases will be reported directly to the patient’s primary care physician and/or to the practice social worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social worker and/or psychiatrist will be consulted immediately to determine level of care; confidentiality may be suspended in event of emergency; participants informed of these limits during consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No FDA-regulated intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: The study will not use an FDA-regulated intervention (answer 'No' to 'Will the study use an FDA-regulated intervention?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 4.6 indicates 'No' and includes a placeholder to describe IND/IDE availability if 'Yes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study team structure and recruitment facilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary team members include PI, primary mentor, co-mentors, medical directors of participating sites, and a research assistant; Drs. Adelman and Bowles will facilitate recruitment of clinicians and caregivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating sites include WCM and VNSNY with VNSNY serving over 6,000 racially diverse hospice patients annually; all data centrally stored at WCM.
